rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent stepped mass in all four views, so the core gesture is legible and repair is clean. However, it behaves more like a compact stacked object than a neighborhood-living building with an active ground threshold. The blue access edge is not answered by a clearly public void or entry seam; the notch/cave logic is too small and visually buried, and the mass remains largely sealed at grade. The stepped silhouette is acceptable as a sectional move, but here it feels closer to generic tiering than a program-driven public section. Because the visible mass does not convincingly support the required active frontage and public-ground relationship, program_fit_hard_pass fails.
